title: Hosted API unit cost deep dive and optimization plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a working deep-dive into per-token COGS and margin by model and region for Hosted API. The goal is to (1) surface where we lose margin today, (2) quantify realistic wins from batching/quantization/region routing, and (3) propose an actionable optimization roadmap for Q2.

Summary findings (short):
- Baseline blended compute + infra COGS per 1k tokens ranges from $0.012 to $0.092 depending on model and region.
- Largest levers: model selection (quantized variants), batching policies, prefix/KV caching for common prompts, and region routing for egress-heavy inference.
- Quick win: enforce default batch size=8 on rw-3-medium and enable prefix cache TTL=30s for assistant-chat route => ~18-25% COGS reduction for that traffic class.

Assumptions used for calculations (explicit):
- Token definition: 1 token ~= 4 characters; unit normalized to 1k tokens for pricing.
- GPU amortized cost (including power, driver infra, orchestration) per GPU-hour: us-west: $2.75, eu-west: $3.10, ap-southeast: $3.60. These are after reserved capacity discounts.
- Throughput (tokens/s) per model single GPU: rw-3-small: 15k t/s, rw-3-medium: 7k t/s, llama2-13b: 4k t/s, mistral-7b: 6k t/s (baseline fp16). Quantized 4-bit improves throughput ~1.25x and lowers GPU memory pressure.
- Network egress cost (per 1k tokens): us-west: $0.0012, eu-west: $0.0015, ap-southeast: $0.0021.
- Overhead (control plane + storage + monitoring) allocated as $0.0009 per 1k tokens.
- Pricing to customer for text generation (example tiers used for margin calc): $0.10 / 1k tokens for standard model; $0.22 / 1k tokens for high-quality model.

rw-3-medium,us-west,$0.036,$0.0012,$0.0009,$0.0381,$0.10,61.9%
rw-3-medium,eu-west,$0.040,$0.0015,$0.0009,$0.0424,$0.10,57.6%

Notes on table: compute_cogs includes amortized GPU + scheduler overhead divided by tokens/s. Table is intentionally conservative on throughput.

Detailed observations:
1) Region delta matters for mid+ large models: moving 25% of rw-3-medium volume from ap-southeast -> us-west reduces blended COGS by ~6.5% for that slice (egress + GPU cost delta).
2) Quantization profile adoption: for rw-3-medium quantized-4 yields ~28% compute COGS reduction in testing but we observe a 1.8% signal-quality regression on our AMI prompt set. That implies we should gate rollouts with quality budgets per customer.
3) Batching exponential returns but with latency trade-offs: increasing average batch size from 1.8 -> 6 gives ~38% lower compute per-token; beyond 8 the latency SLOs for interactive apps start to degrade.
4) Cacheable patterns: 24% of assistant CHAT requests share first 64-token prefixes (system + user scaffolding). Prefix/KV caching reduces effective tokens generated by the model for repeated prompts and shows ~45% effective cost reduction on that surface when cache hit rate > 60%.

Optimization recommendations (prioritized):
- Priority 1 (fast infra wins, measurable):
  * Deploy prefix/KV cache for assistant-chat route with 30s default TTL + per-customer opt-out. Target hit rate baseline >= 45%. Instrument hit rate / token savings dashboards (obs-reqs ENG-1565). Estimated COGS reduction for route: 18-30%.
  * Enforce default batching policy: min_batch=4, target_batch=8 for rw-3-medium and rw-3-small when latency SLO allows. Add latency backpressure and per-route policy. Expected blended compute savings 20-40% depending on traffic shape.
- Priority 2 (pricing & routing):
  * Introduce region-aware routing for non-compliance-sensitive customers: route to lowest-cost region that meets latency SLO by default. Add a "preferred-region" flag in tenant config. Expected blended platform savings 3-7%.
  * Launch a quantized-variant price tier ("fast-quant" at -20% price) with explicit QA SLA. Only eligible for customers who accept minor quality delta and can be force-degraded.
- Priority 3 (product/price changes):
  * Introduce model-tiered pricing with clear per-1k matrix and a new "economy" model family backed by rw-3-small/quant. Aim: move 30% of low-quality-sensitive traffic to economy within 2 quarters.
  * Add per-route cost-estimates on Console and SDK (estimate tokens * model COGS) so teams can self-optimize.

Risks and guardrails:
- Quality regressions from quantization can create support/CS load. Require canary on 1-2 customers for 2 weeks with automated rollback on eval regressions >2% absolute on our synthetic eval suite.
- Batching changes affect P99 tail latency; we must add safe fallbacks to prioritize interactive traffic (token-bucket to bypass batching if latency spike).
- Prefix cache correctness: must ensure variable system messages and dynamic per-request metadata are not cached. Implementation MUST honor per-request nonce keys and TTLs.

Experiment plan (3-week sprints):
Week 1: Implement prefix cache for assistant-chat on canary (10% traffic), add hit/miss instrumentation, record delta in tokens generated.
Week 2: Implement default batching policy in serving runtime for rw-3-medium path and canary 15% traffic. Monitor P50/P95/P99 latency and throughput.
Week 3: Rollout regional routing as opt-in for non-enterprise tenants; sample costs and latencies for 2 weeks before widening.
Success metrics: 
- Platform-level COGS/1k decreases by 10% within 6 weeks of combined batching+cache rollout (measured net of traffic mix).
- No more than 1% increase in support cases referencing hallucinations or quality from customers on quantized tiers during canary.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Need accurate per-GPU amortization numbers from Finance (ticket FIN-1982) — current numbers are provisional.
- Validate network egress costs for multi-cloud region peering with infra (ENG-1604).
- Add per-tenant historical prompt duplication rates to better estimate cacheable volume.

Appendix: short worked example (rw-3-medium, us-west)
- Single GPU throughput: 7k t/s -> 25.2M tokens/hour. GPU cost $2.75/hr -> compute cost per 1k tokens = 2.75 / 25200 = $0.000109 (note: simplified, real runtime overheads make effective compute_cogs higher; above table uses conservative overhead multipliers to match production measurements).
- After scheduler/standing buffers/idle we estimate effective compute_cogs = $0.036 / 1k tokens. With network + overhead total = $0.0381.

Contact / next steps:
- Please review numbers and leave inline comments. I want Finance (Miguel), SRE (Ethan) and Applied ML (Sana) to sanity-check the throughput and quality tradeoffs.
- If approved, ENG: circle back on canary flags and telemetry requirements (ENG-1565, ENG-1604).

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Consider offering "burst credits" to customers when we route them to lower-cost regions (sticky credits can offset initial latency concerns).
- Explore per-customer model pinning price premium for enterprise customers that require fixed SLA.

End of doc (working).
